newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares rise at start of settlement period.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares rise at start of settlement period.

text.p: Delhi shares climbed higher in early trade on Monday as traders ignored turbulent political developments in India's ruling United Front to make fresh purchases at the start of a new settlement period, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index was 10.07 points higher at 920.53 points after 30 minutes of trade.
Brokers said strong buying by foreign and domestic financial institutions helped lift prices.

"Massive purchases by foreign institutional investors show the market has ignored an adverse political situation following a split in the Janata Dal, a constituent of the ruling United Front government," said Harish Malhotra of brokers Malhotra Financial Consultants.

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's Janata Dal party split on Saturday, but breakaway leader Laloo Prasad Yadav assured continued support to the ruling 15-party United Front alliance, which runs a minority government.
Reliance Industries gained 10.70 rupees to 365.25 on strong buying by foreign investors, brokers said.
ITC surged 34.50 rupees to 561.50 on speculative buying as the share will be in a no-delivery period for the next two settlements, they said.
Larsen and Toubro increased 2.75 rupees to 258.00.
